Definition: of Hebrew origin (H894); Babylon, the capitol of Chaldæa (literally or figuratively (as a type of tyranny)):-- Babylon.
BiblicalUsage: Babylon is the city of the exile and the city of the last days: Matthew counts it in the genealogy — they were carried away to Babylon — Stephen says God removed them into Babylon, and Peter sends greetings from the church at Babylon, while Revelation says Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen. The same city, first as judgment and last as the fall of the world itself.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Babylon falls twice — once to Persia, and once at the end of the age — and I hold that the church which greets me from Babylon in Peter's letter is the proof that God keeps his people even there.
